questions.prompt: Convert 3 metres into centimetres.

questions.title: Question 1(b): Division by Powers of 10
questions.prompt: Work out 3400 ÷ 1000
modelSteps: Dividing by 1000 shifts the decimal point 3 places to the left.

modelSteps: BIDMAS Priority: Division comes before Subtraction.

questions.title: Question 2: Brick Wall Delivery Estimation
questions.prompt:
Aaron is building a brick wall. The wall will need 1025 bricks. The weight of each brick is 2.89 kg. Aaron will pay a delivery charge if the total weight of the bricks is over 2500 kg.

Use estimation to work out if you think Aaron will need to pay the delivery charge. You must show your working.
modelSteps: Step 1: Round values to 1 significant figure for estimation.
Step 2: Estimate total weight: 1000 × 3 kg = 3000 kg.
Step 3: Compare with delivery threshold: 3000 kg > 2500 kg.
Conclusion: Yes, Aaron will need to pay the delivery charge [A1].

questions.title: Question 3(a): Perimeter of Rectangular Field
questions.prompt:
A farmer has a rectangular field. The field is 300 m long and 200 m wide.

Calculate the perimeter of the field.
modelSteps: Perimeter formula for rectangle: 2 × (Length + Width) or sum of all 4 sides.

questions.title: Question 3(b): Field Area & Fertiliser Quantity
questions.prompt:
The farmer puts fertiliser on the field. He needs 1 kg of fertiliser for every 40 m² of field.

How many kilograms of fertiliser does the farmer need?
modelSteps: Step 1: Calculate total area of the field: Area = Length × Width = 300 × 200 = 60,000 m² [M1]
Step 2: Divide by application rate: 60,000 ÷ 40 = 1,500 kg [A1]

questions.prompt:

Write the ratio of the number of cups of tea to the number of cups of coffee in its simplest form.

questions.title: Question 2: Office Chairs & 20% VAT
questions.prompt:
Sam is a manager in an office. She wants to buy 14 new chairs. Each chair costs £73. Sam will also be charged 20% VAT.

Work out the total amount Sam will pay for the 14 chairs including VAT.

questions.title: Question 3: Rectangular Garden & Pond Grass Seed
questions.prompt:
Here is a garden and a pond. The garden and the pond are rectangular.
• Garden dimensions: 14 m by 9 m
• Pond dimensions: 3.8 m by 2.4 m

Kayla is covering the garden with grass seed. She will not put any grass seed in the pond. One box of grass seed covers 15 m² of garden.

Work out the number of boxes of grass seed Kayla needs to cover the garden.
modelSteps: Step 1: Total area of garden = 14 × 9 = 126 m² [M1]
Step 3: Area needing grass seed = 126 – 9.12 = 116.88 m²
Step 4: Number of boxes required = 116.88 ÷ 15 = 7.792... boxes [M1]
Rounding: Kayla cannot buy a fraction of a box, so round up to 8 whole boxes.

questions.title: Question 4: Temperature Formula Conversion
questions.prompt:
Dave is going on holiday to Madrid. The temperature tomorrow in Madrid will be 21°C.

Dave uses this rule to convert °C to °F:
"Multiply the temperature in °C by 1.8 then add 32"

Work out the temperature in Madrid in °F.

questions.title: Question 5: Call Centre Phone Calls Frequency
questions.prompt:
Kai works in a call centre. The table shows the number of phone calls he receives each day:

• Monday: 240
• Tuesday: 140
• Wednesday: 185
• Thursday: 80
• Friday: 225

Calculate the total number of calls received and the daily range of phone calls.
modelSteps: Step 2: Range = Highest – Lowest = 240 – 80 = 160 calls [M1, A1]

questions.title: Question 6: Bakery Flour Mean & Mass Conversion
questions.prompt:
Seenal is a baker. She buys flour in 50 kg bags. The table shows the number of 50 kg bags of flour she used to make loaves in each of the last 4 weeks:
• Week 1: 12 bags
• Week 2: 16 bags
• Week 3: 13 bags
• Week 4: 15 bags

Seenal will make 2400 loaves in week 5. Each of these loaves will need 250 g of flour.

Seenal works out the weekly mean number of 50 kg bags of flour used in these 5 weeks. Work out the weekly mean number of 50 kg bags.
modelSteps: Step 1: Calculate flour needed in Week 5: 2400 × 250 g = 600,000 g [M1]
Convert grams to kilograms: 600,000 g ÷ 1000 = 600 kg
Convert to 50 kg bags: 600 ÷ 50 = 12 bags for Week 5 [M1]
Step 2: Total bags over 5 weeks: 12 + 16 + 13 + 15 + 12 = 68 bags

questions.title: Question 7: Slide Dimension & Garden Clearance
questions.prompt:
Gordon buys a new slide for his garden. His garden measures 6 m by 7 m.
The space for the slide must have a clearance border of at least 1.5 m from the fence on all sides.
If the base of the slide is 2 m by 3.5 m, calculate the total space required including clearance, and decide if it will fit safely in the garden.
modelSteps: Step 1: Add 1.5 m border on each side to length: 3.5 + 1.5 + 1.5 = 6.5 m [M1]
Step 2: Add 1.5 m border on each side to width: 2.0 + 1.5 + 1.5 = 5.0 m [M1]
Step 3: Total required dimensions: 6.5 m by 5.0 m.
Step 4: Compare with garden dimensions (7 m by 6 m): 6.5 m ≤ 7 m and 5.0 m ≤ 6 m.
Conclusion: Yes, the slide and clearance area will fit safely [A1].

questions.title: Question 8: Equal Grouped Frequency Distribution
questions.prompt:
Belinda asks 20 people how many hours they spent exercising last month. The data is:
4, 12, 18, 7, 2, 15, 9, 14, 6, 11, 20, 3, 8, 16, 5, 10, 19, 1, 13, 17.

Belinda wants to show these results in a frequency table with 4 equal groups, starting at 1 hour and ending at 20 hours.
Work out the width of each group and state the frequency of the first group (1 to 5 hours).
modelSteps: Step 1: Group range: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 hours per group.
Step 2: Tally values in group 1–5: 4, 2, 3, 5, 1 = 5 people [M1]

questions.title: Question 9: Cuboid Container Capacity & Length
questions.prompt:
Dennis is making a container for tomato plants. The container will be in the shape of a cuboid.
• Height = 40 cm
• Width = 55 cm
• Capacity of container = 180 litres
• 1 litre = 1000 cm³

Work out the length of the container. Give your answer to the nearest whole centimetre.
modelSteps: Step 1: Convert litres to cm³: 180 × 1000 = 180,000 cm³ [M1]
Step 4: Round to nearest whole centimetre: 81.818... ≈ 82 cm [A1]

questions.title: Question 10(a): 3D Shapes & Geometric Nets
questions.prompt:
A triangular prism has 5 faces: 2 congruent triangular bases and 3 rectangular faces.
How many edges and vertices does a triangular prism have?
modelSteps: Edges: 3 on bottom triangle + 3 on top triangle + 3 vertical = 9 edges [B1]
Vertices: 3 at bottom + 3 at top = 6 vertices [B1]

questions.title: Question 10(b): Plan View of a Cylinder
questions.prompt: A solid cylinder is placed upright on a flat table. What 2D geometric shape is the plan view (view from directly above)?
modelSteps: The plan view of an upright cylinder viewed from directly above is a circle [B1].

questions.title: Question 11(a): House Deposit Percentage Calculation
questions.prompt:
James wants to buy a house. The price of the house is a quarter of a million pounds (£250,000).
James has to pay a deposit for the house. The deposit is 15% of the price of the house.

James already has £18,500 saved and his family will lend him £15,000.
Does James have enough money to pay the deposit? Show working to support your decision.
modelSteps: Step 1: Calculate house price: A quarter of a million = £250,000 [M1]
Step 3: Calculate James's total available funds: £18,500 + £15,000 = £33,500 [M1]
Conclusion: No, James does not have enough money (he is short by £4,000) [A1].

questions.title: Question 11(b): Percentage Calculation Reverse Check
questions.prompt: Show a check of your percentage calculation for Question 11(a).
